practiceNotes: This is a proposed prerequisite graph, not an applied curriculum or a certification of competence.

Use spaced repetition for definitions, representations, assumptions, mechanisms, counterexamples and method selection. Require separate assessment of proofs, derivations, code, experimental work and extended modeling.

Advance through prerequisite decks by demonstrated competence, including their performance tasks; outcome annotations explain dependencies but do not authorize skipping the rest of a prerequisite deck.

Wet chemistry, biological cultures, radiation, lasers, electrical apparatus and animal work require suitable facilities, risk assessment, supervision and applicable authorization. These conditions are not represented as already satisfied.

Human-participant studies and identifiable biological or behavioral data require applicable consent, privacy protections and ethics review. Use approved public or synthetic datasets when authorization is unavailable.
Security exercises must use isolated, explicitly authorized systems. Embedded and robotic exercises should begin in simulation or low-energy test environments.
Maintain reproducible notebooks, versioned code, uncertainty records and negative results. Assess transfer with unfamiliar examples rather than relying only on familiar flashcard prompts.

outcomes.description: Determine coordination geometry, oxidation state, electron count and stereoisomerism.
Use specified ligand-field splitting models to predict spin, magnetism and qualitative spectra.
Distinguish thermodynamic stability from kinetic inertness and analyze ligand-substitution pathways.

practice: Interpret complex structures, spectra and exchange data and compare competing bonding explanations.

includes: Sampling and method validation; chromatography and extraction theory; gravimetric and titrimetric quantitative analysis.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Analytical Chemistry

outcomes.description: Design sampling, calibration and validation procedures and calculate detection limits and uncertainty.
Explain and optimize separation selectivity, partitioning and chromatographic resolution.
Perform gravimetric and titrimetric analyses with equilibrium and interference corrections.

practice: Validate an analytical method using blanks, standards, spikes and an independently characterized sample.

includes: Operational UV-visible and infrared models; elementary nuclear-spin resonance and chemical shifts; ionization, mass spectra and fragmentation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Instrumental Chemical Analysis

outcomes.description: Use explicitly taught photon and vibrational models to interpret optical spectra and Beer-Lambert quantification.
Use a bounded spin-transition model to interpret elementary NMR shifts, integration and coupling.
Interpret mass spectra using ionization, isotope patterns and chemically justified fragmentation.

practice: Determine unknown structures from complementary spectra and validate quantitative instrument measurements.

includes: Atomic electronic structure; molecular orbital construction and symmetry; variational bonding and elementary many-electron approximations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry

outcomes.description: Derive atomic orbital and electron-configuration consequences with electron-interaction approximations made explicit.
Construct molecular orbitals and use symmetry and occupancy to predict bonding and reactivity.
Apply variational and linear-combination methods and assess their limitations for molecular energies.

practice: Derive small-basis molecular calculations and compare quantum bonding models with chemical evidence.

includes: Partial molar properties and chemical potentials; activities and nonideal mixtures; phase diagrams and multicomponent equilibrium.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics

outcomes.description: Derive chemical-potential and partial-molar relations and connect them to reaction equilibrium.
Calculate activities and mixture properties using ideal and specified nonideal solution models.
Construct and interpret phase diagrams and derive coexistence and stability conditions.

practice: Derive mixture identities and solve nonideal reaction and phase-equilibrium problems.

includes: Molecular rotational, vibrational and electronic partitions; statistical reaction equilibrium; molecular fluctuations and response.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Statistical Thermodynamics

outcomes.description: Construct molecular partition functions from explicit energy spectra and justify separability approximations.
Derive equilibrium constants and chemical potentials from molecular state counting.
Calculate molecular heat capacities and response functions and explain approximation breakdowns.

practice: Derive molecular thermodynamic predictions and compare high- and low-temperature limits.

includes: Coupled reaction networks and timescale approximations; transition-state theory; collision and potential-energy-surface dynamics.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Reaction Dynamics

outcomes.description: Derive network ODEs and justify steady-state and pre-equilibrium reductions using timescales.
Derive transition-state rate expressions and assess entropy, tunneling and recrossing limitations.
Analyze collision energetics and reaction trajectories on specified potential-energy surfaces.

practice: Derive reduced mechanisms and solve rate-theory problems with competing dynamical approximations.

includes: Electrode potentials and electrochemical cells; Butler-Volmer kinetics as an explicit interfacial model; diffusion and migration in simple geometries.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Electrochemistry

outcomes.description: Derive Nernst relations and calculate cell potentials, equilibria and thermodynamic efficiencies.
Interpret polarization and exchange-current data using stated charge-transfer assumptions.
Derive one-dimensional steady diffusion currents and distinguish transport from kinetic limitations.

practice: Analyze battery, corrosion and voltammetric datasets with explicit thermodynamic and transport checks.

includes: Crystal structures and diffraction geometry; point defects and nonstoichiometry; solid-state synthesis and structure-property assessment.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Materials Chemistry

outcomes.description: Index elementary crystal structures and diffraction patterns using lattice and reciprocal-vector geometry.
Use defect and charge-balance models to predict nonstoichiometry and ionic or electronic compensation.
Design ceramic, solution and vapor synthesis routes and relate processing to material structure.

practice: Interpret diffraction and phase data and propose synthesis routes with defect and stability predictions.

includes: Step and chain polymerization; molecular-weight distributions; polymer architecture, transitions and structure-property relations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Polymer Chemistry

outcomes.description: Derive elementary step- and chain-growth relationships and predict architectural consequences of mechanisms.
Calculate molecular-weight averages and dispersity from distributions and ideal polymerization models.
Relate architecture, intermolecular forces and processing to glass transitions, crystallinity and mechanical response.

practice: Analyze polymerization and molecular-weight data and design materials for specified property constraints.

includes: Surface energy and capillarity; adsorption isotherms and surface kinetics; colloidal interactions and aggregation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Chemistry at interfaces and in dispersions.
decks.title: Surface and Colloid Chemistry

outcomes.description: Derive capillary and interfacial equilibrium relations and interpret wetting phenomena.
Derive elementary adsorption isotherms and distinguish equilibrium coverage from surface-reaction rates.
Use explicitly specified electrostatic and dispersion potentials to predict colloidal stability and aggregation.

practice: Analyze adsorption and stability data and compare competing models for emulsions and catalytic surfaces.

includes: Metal-carbon bonding and electron counting; elementary organometallic steps; homogeneous catalytic cycles and mechanistic selectivity.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organometallic Chemistry and Catalysis

outcomes.description: Analyze organometallic bonding, electron counts and ligand effects on reactive configurations.
Predict oxidative addition, reductive elimination, insertion and elimination steps with mechanistic constraints.
Construct and assess catalytic cycles using kinetics, selectivity and catalyst-deactivation evidence.

practice: Reconstruct catalytic mechanisms and design experiments distinguishing resting states and rate-limiting steps.

includes: Asymmetric synthesis; orbital-symmetry and pericyclic strategy; complex-route efficiency and sustainability.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Synthetic Strategy

outcomes.description: Design stereoselective transformations using substrate, reagent and catalyst control models.
Derive orbital-symmetry predictions for pericyclic reactions and incorporate them into synthetic routes.
Compare complex routes using selectivity, step economy, robustness, waste and mechanistic uncertainty.

practice: Defend alternative syntheses of a complex target using primary reaction evidence.

includes: Protein, nucleic-acid, carbohydrate and lipid chemistry; folding and binding; enzyme mechanisms and Michaelis-Menten models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Shared chemical foundations of living matter.
decks.title: Biomolecules and Enzymes

outcomes.description: Relate biomolecular functional groups and stereochemistry to polymer structure, interactions and chemical reactivity.
Explain protein folding and binding using energetic, structural and environmental evidence.
Construct acid-base, covalent, acyl-transfer and redox enzyme mechanisms with valid electron flow.
Derive the steady-state Michaelis-Menten relation algebraically and interpret inhibition and kinetic data.

practice: Analyze enzyme mechanisms, folding perturbations and kinetic datasets with explicit alternative explanations.

includes: Chemical probes and bioorthogonal reactions; target engagement and causal perturbation; structure-activity, selectivity and elementary disposition models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Biology

outcomes.description: Design molecular probes with justified reactivity, labeling specificity and controls.
Distinguish target binding, functional inhibition and off-target effects using orthogonal assays.
Interpret structure-activity series and bounded absorption, distribution and stability measurements.

practice: Develop a probe-validation dossier separating chemical selectivity, target engagement and biological causation.

includes: Air, water and soil speciation; partitioning and algebraic compartment balances; pollutant measurement and source assessment.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry

outcomes.description: Predict environmentally relevant acid-base, redox, sorption and complexation effects on chemical form.
Construct steady compartment balances and estimate residence times, partitioning and degradation under stated models.
Design environmental sampling and analytical controls and distinguish source evidence from exposure claims.

practice: Analyze a watershed or urban-air case using chemical speciation, measured concentrations and mass balances.

includes: Decay and activation chemistry; radiochemical separation and counting; isotope tracing, dating and radiation effects.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Chemical use and analysis of nuclear transformations.
decks.title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry

outcomes.description: Calculate coupled decay and activation yields and predict chemical consequences of nuclear transformations.
Design radiochemical separation and counting analyses with efficiency, background and contamination controls.
Evaluate isotope tracing and dating models and distinguish chemical fractionation from nuclear effects.

practice: Analyze authorized or simulated activation, tracing and decay datasets with full uncertainty and safety plans.

includes: Hartree-Fock and density-functional methods; basis sets and molecular calculations; convergence, correlation and validation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Computational Electronic Structure

outcomes.description: Derive self-consistent-field equations and explain density-functional and correlation approximations.
Perform basis-controlled energy, geometry and property calculations with documented numerical settings.
Assess convergence, basis error, correlation limitations and comparison with chemical evidence.

practice: Implement a small self-consistent-field calculation and benchmark a molecular prediction across approximation choices.

includes: Classical force fields and molecular dynamics; equilibrium Monte Carlo; sampling, finite-size and force-field validation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Simulation

outcomes.description: Implement molecular dynamics with force fields, constraints, periodic boundaries and appropriate integration checks.
Derive detailed-balance Monte Carlo moves and calculate equilibrium averages and free-energy differences.
Assess equilibration, autocorrelation, finite-size effects and model inadequacy in molecular simulations.

practice: Implement and validate a small molecular simulator and compare dynamic and Monte Carlo estimates.

includes: Rotational and vibrational transitions; electronic spectroscopy and selection rules; spin Hamiltonians, pulses and relaxation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Spectroscopy

outcomes.description: Derive rotational and vibrational spectra and selection rules from molecular Hamiltonians.
Calculate elementary electronic transition strengths and explain vibronic structure and broadening.
Analyze spin Hamiltonians, pulse evolution and relaxation in elementary magnetic-resonance experiments.

practice: Derive and interpret spectra and design pulse or polarization measurements that distinguish molecular models.

includes: Excited-state surfaces and nonradiative pathways; quantum yields and photokinetics; photosensitization and photochemical control.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Photochemistry

outcomes.description: Explain radiative and nonradiative pathways using state symmetry, surfaces and coupling mechanisms.
Derive photokinetic networks and estimate lifetimes, branching ratios and quantum yields.
Design photochemical or photosensitized transformations with justified wavelength, quenching and control choices.

practice: Analyze time-resolved photochemical data and compare mechanistic models of competing excited-state reactions.

includes: Atmospheric radical and multiphase mechanisms; photolysis-coupled box models; sensitivity and mechanism reduction.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Advanced chemical modeling of atmospheric change.
decks.title: Atmospheric Reaction Networks

Implement stiff atmospheric box models with prescribed transport and radiation inputs.
Evaluate sensitivity and reduced mechanisms while preserving key chemical observables and limitations.

practice: Reproduce a bounded atmospheric chemistry study and test mechanism sensitivity to emissions and photolysis.

includes: Cells, organisms and biological scales; inheritance and evolution as introductory explanations; observation, hypothesis and evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Living Systems

outcomes.description: Distinguish cellular, organismal, population and ecosystem organization and explain emergent biological functions.
Explain inheritance, variation and natural selection conceptually without teleological reasoning.
Distinguish observations, hypotheses, mechanisms and evidence, including alternatives and uncertainty.

practice: Compare organisms and evaluate competing explanations using observations and simple evidence dossiers.

includes: Light microscopy and scale; field sampling and identification records; specimen handling, contamination and biological ethics.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biological Observation and Sampling

Design elementary quadrat, transect and specimen sampling with explicit detection and selection limitations.
Maintain specimen provenance and follow taught contamination, humane-handling and containment procedures.

practice: Produce a calibrated microscopy portfolio and a documented, minimally invasive field-sampling study.

includes: Biological controls and replication; inferential comparisons and causal limitations; reproducible protocols and data records.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Design and interpretation of biological investigations.
decks.title: Experimental Biology

Interpret effect estimates and uncertainty while identifying confounding and alternative biological mechanisms.
Produce reproducible protocols, raw-data records and transparent reports including exclusions and negative results.

practice: Design and analyze a controlled growth or observational field investigation and critique its causal limits.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cell Biology

outcomes.description: Relate cellular structures and organelles to transport, synthesis, energy conversion and information processing.
Explain membrane organization and selective permeability using molecular polarity and compartment models.
Explain chromosome segregation, mitosis and cell-cycle checkpoints and predict elementary division failures.

practice: Interpret cell images and perturbation cases and construct mechanistic compartment diagrams.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genetics

Infer linkage and recombination maps from crosses and identify limits of mapping resolution.
Explain chromosome-number and structural variation and predict transmission and phenotypic consequences.

practice: Solve cross and pedigree problems and distinguish genetic models using supplied offspring data.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Mechanisms and history of biological change.
decks.title: Evolutionary Biology

outcomes.description: Distinguish evolutionary mechanisms and predict qualitative changes under specified population conditions.
Explain reproductive isolation and compare speciation hypotheses using genetic, ecological and fossil evidence.
Construct and interpret elementary phylogenies and distinguish homology, convergence and ancestral-state uncertainty.

practice: Evaluate adaptive and nonadaptive explanations and reconstruct small phylogenies from character evidence.

includes: Taxonomic and phylogenetic classification; major microbial and eukaryotic lineages; diversity estimation and identification uncertainty.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Organismal diversity in an evolutionary framework.
decks.title: Biodiversity and Systematics

outcomes.description: Use keys and phylogenetic classification while distinguishing operational taxa and species concepts.
Compare major bacterial, archaeal and eukaryotic lineages using distinctive structures and life histories.
Estimate and compare sampled diversity while accounting for effort, detection and taxonomic uncertainty.

practice: Construct an annotated local or digital biodiversity collection and justify classifications and sampling limits.

includes: Microbial growth and metabolic diversity; bacterial and archaeal structure; ecological and pathogenic interactions; culture and susceptibility methods.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Microorganisms as organisms and interacting populations.
decks.title: Microbiology

outcomes.description: Calculate microbial growth and dilution relationships and explain nutrient and environmental limitations.
Compare bacterial and archaeal structures, metabolism and genetic exchange using organismal evidence.
Explain microbial symbiosis, biofilms, pathogenesis and antimicrobial-resistance mechanisms.
Design aseptic culture, enumeration and susceptibility assays with valid controls and containment.

practice: Analyze or safely perform nonpathogenic growth and susceptibility investigations with contamination controls.

includes: Viral genome strategies and replication; host range, persistence and evolution; infectivity, replication and antiviral assays.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Viruses and their host-dependent life cycles.
decks.title: Virology

outcomes.description: Compare viral replication strategies and explain entry, genome expression, assembly and release.
Analyze host range, persistence, recombination and evolutionary escape using viral evidence.
Interpret plaque, molecular and neutralization assays while distinguishing infectivity from genome abundance.

practice: Reconstruct viral life cycles and analyze approved or simulated infection and antiviral datasets.

includes: Plant tissues and organs; alternation of generations and reproduction; water, mineral and assimilate transport; environmental physiology using bounded models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Plant Biology

outcomes.description: Relate plant tissue and organ organization to growth and terrestrial adaptation.
Compare plant life cycles and explain reproductive and dispersal strategies.
Apply explicitly taught water-potential and source-sink models to plant transport and stomatal behavior.
Interpret plant responses to light, nutrients, water and stress using controlled evidence.

practice: Compare plant anatomy and life cycles and conduct controlled germination or transpiration investigations.

includes: Fungal growth, nutrition and reproduction; protist cellular innovations and life cycles; parasitism, endosymbiosis and mutualism.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Fungi and Protists

Compare major protist cellular innovations, locomotion, trophic strategies and life cycles.
Analyze fungal and protist symbioses and parasitic life histories using ecological and cellular evidence.

practice: Build comparative life-cycle explanations and identify organisms from microscopy and ecological evidence.

includes: Comparative animal body organization; tissue histology; organ architecture and structure-function relationships.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Comparative Animal Anatomy

outcomes.description: Compare symmetry, segmentation, body cavities and support systems across representative animals.
Identify epithelial, connective, muscular and neural tissues from calibrated histological evidence.
Relate digestive, circulatory, respiratory, excretory, endocrine and reproductive architectures to functional constraints.

practice: Produce comparative anatomical and histological analyses using models, images and authorized specimens.

includes: Diffusion, osmosis and carrier transport; membrane potentials and excitable membranes; feedback, signaling and homeostatic set points.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cellular Physiology and Homeostasis

outcomes.description: Apply explicitly defined diffusion, osmotic and transporter models to cellular flux and steady states.
Calculate equilibrium potentials with the stated Nernst model and explain action-potential mechanisms and limits.
Construct feedback models and distinguish regulated variables, effectors, compensation and control failure.

practice: Interpret transport and electrophysiological traces and diagnose failures in simple homeostatic systems.

decks.description: Integrated transport of gases through animals.
decks.title: Cardiorespiratory Physiology

Analyze ventilation, diffusion and gas transport using explicit partial-pressure and binding models.
Integrate circulation and respiration to explain exercise, hypoxia, shock and compensatory limits.

practice: Solve oxygen-delivery and pressure-flow cases and interpret noninvasive physiological recordings.

includes: Filtration and renal clearance; tubular transport and concentration; water, electrolyte and acid-base regulation and failure.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Renal and Osmoregulatory Physiology

outcomes.description: Calculate filtration, excretion and clearance and relate them to nephron transport mechanisms.
Explain countercurrent concentration and hormonal water and electrolyte regulation across animal strategies.
Analyze renal acid-base compensation and distinguish elementary renal, respiratory and metabolic disturbances.

practice: Solve renal balance and clearance cases and compare osmoregulatory adaptations in different environments.

includes: Hormonal feedback and energy regulation; digestion and absorption; reproductive endocrine axes and their failures.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Hormonal coordination of nutrition and reproduction.
decks.title: Endocrine and Digestive Physiology

outcomes.description: Analyze endocrine axes and distinguish primary, secondary and feedback-driven dysfunction.
Explain digestive secretion, motility and nutrient absorption and predict consequences of malabsorption.
Explain gametogenesis, reproductive cycles and hormonal coordination of reproduction and development.

practice: Interpret hormone and nutrient profiles and construct mechanistic feedback explanations for physiological disturbances.

includes: Synaptic and neuromuscular transmission; neural circuits and coding; sensory and motor systems; plasticity, learning and experimental inference.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: From excitable cells to neural systems.
decks.title: Neuroscience

outcomes.description: Explain synaptic integration, neurotransmission and neuromuscular activation from cellular mechanisms.
Interpret elementary neural coding and circuit motifs using recordings and perturbations.
Trace sensory processing and motor control through representative pathways and lesion evidence.
Explain cellular plasticity and evaluate evidence linking neural change to learning and memory.

practice: Analyze neural recordings and lesion or perturbation studies without inferring causation from correlation alone.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Behavioral Biology

outcomes.description: Distinguish developmental, physiological, functional and phylogenetic explanations of behavior.
Analyze foraging, mating, communication and social behavior using explicit fitness and tradeoff models.
Design ethograms and behavioral experiments that control observer bias, dependence and alternative explanations.

practice: Conduct approved observational behavior coding and compare competing adaptive and learning hypotheses.

includes: Population demography using discrete balances; species interactions and communities; energy flow, productivity and environmental gradients.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecology

outcomes.description: Analyze life tables and discrete population balances and explain density dependence and dispersal.
Explain competition, predation, mutualism and community assembly using observational and experimental evidence.
Compare productivity, trophic transfer and nutrient limitation across terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.

practice: Analyze field population and community datasets and construct accountable ecosystem energy budgets.

Estimate simple ecological models and assess identifiability, residual structure and out-of-sample predictions.

practice: Derive and analyze population models and compare their predictions with supplied longitudinal data.

includes: Carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus cycles; terrestrial and aquatic compartment budgets; disturbance, climate feedback and ecosystem limitation.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecosystem Biogeochemistry

Construct and solve ecosystem mass-balance and residence-time models with explicit boundaries.
Evaluate disturbance and climate-feedback hypotheses using flux, stoichiometric and ecological evidence.

practice: Construct a watershed or ecosystem nutrient budget and assess sensitivity to disturbance and missing fluxes.

includes: Extinction drivers and fragmentation; conservation decisions under uncertainty; restoration design and monitoring.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular Genetics

Analyze regulatory circuits, chromatin and epigenetic mechanisms using causal molecular evidence.

practice: Interpret molecular perturbation datasets and distinguish competing information-processing mechanisms.

decks.subject: biology

Plan cloning, expression and genome-editing experiments and verify intended and unintended changes.
Choose and validate molecular abundance, localization and interaction assays with orthogonal controls.

practice: Design and, where authorized, execute a molecular perturbation study with sequence and assay validation.

includes: Central carbon and biosynthetic pathways; respiratory and photosynthetic energy conversion; metabolic integration and regulation.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Metabolism and Bioenergetics

Predict metabolic responses to nutrient, hormonal and environmental changes and identify consequences of pathway defects.

practice: Solve metabolic accounting and perturbation problems and explain pathway-level physiological failures.

includes: Cell fate and positional patterning; morphogenesis and tissue interactions; lineage, transplantation and genetic perturbation evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Developmental Biology

Relate cell behaviors and tissue interactions to morphogenesis, organogenesis and developmental defects.
Evaluate lineage tracing, transplantation and perturbation experiments for necessity, sufficiency and developmental timing.

practice: Reconstruct developmental mechanisms from time-resolved and perturbational evidence across model organisms.

includes: Innate recognition and inflammation; adaptive receptor diversity and effector responses; tolerance, hypersensitivity and immunodeficiency; immune assays.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Immunology

Derive adaptive specificity and memory from receptor generation, selection and lymphocyte activation.
Explain tolerance, autoimmunity, hypersensitivity and immunodeficiency through regulatory mechanisms.
Design and interpret antibody, cellular and challenge-response assays with specificity and control checks.

practice: Analyze immune-response and vaccine datasets and distinguish protective responses from immune pathology.

Analyze cancer initiation, progression and resistance as failures of regulation and somatic evolution.
Trace inherited and metabolic defects from molecular lesion to cellular and systemic dysfunction.

practice: Analyze an outbreak and an observational exposure study, separating mechanistic, statistical and causal claims.

decks.title: Population Genetics

practice: Derive allele-frequency models and interpret population data under alternative evolutionary mechanisms.

practice: Implement sequence algorithms and analyze a public genome dataset with independent validation checks.

practice: Reproduce and critically extend a public population or functional genomics analysis.

Relate cytoskeletal assembly and motors to shape, transport and division using quantitative experimental evidence.
Evaluate mechanisms of differentiation, senescence and cell-state switching using causal molecular experiments.

practice: Develop a mechanistic cell-biology proposal with competing models and discriminating perturbations.

Explain meristem regulation, organ patterning and reproductive transitions using developmental evidence.
Evaluate mechanisms of plant stress tolerance, acclimation and growth tradeoffs under controlled conditions.

practice: Design a plant perturbation study linking molecular signaling to developmental and physiological outcomes.

Construct and validate structural ensembles from distance and orientation restraints.
Infer bounded dynamical and exchange models from relaxation and lineshape measurements.

practice: Assign a small public dataset and compare structural and dynamical interpretations with restraint validation.

includes: Genetic circuit and pathway engineering; design-build-test-learn validation; containment, evolutionary stability and responsible engineering.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Synthetic Biology

outcomes.description: Design genetic circuits or metabolic interventions with explicit host-resource and evolutionary constraints.
Plan iterative construction and quantitative validation that distinguishes model, implementation and measurement failures.
Evaluate containment, misuse, ecological and stability risks and propose proportionate safeguards.

practice: Develop a simulation-first engineering proposal and an authorized low-risk validation plan with explicit safeguards.

includes: Physical instruments and calibration; dimensions and scaling; experimental comparison of simple models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Evidence and uncertainty in physical experiments.
decks.title: Physical Measurement

outcomes.description: Select and calibrate elementary physical instruments and document resolution, bias and uncertainty.
Use dimensions, scaling and limiting cases to construct and reject physical models.
Compare measured relationships with predictions using plots, residuals and uncertainty bounds.

practice: Conduct low-risk motion, length and timing experiments and produce a model-comparison report.

includes: Position, velocity and constant acceleration; Newtonian free-body models; elementary energy and momentum conservation.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: An algebraic entry into physical dynamics.
decks.title: Elementary Mechanics

outcomes.description: Interpret motion graphs and solve constant-acceleration and projectile models with consistent coordinates.
Construct free-body diagrams and solve elementary equilibrium and constant-force problems.
Apply algebraic energy and momentum balances and distinguish system boundaries and external transfers.

practice: Solve and test elementary motion models and explain common force and energy misconceptions.

includes: Variable-force particle dynamics; work, impulse and conservation; rigid-body rotation; small oscillations and damping models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Newtonian Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive and solve particle equations for variable forces and elementary orbital or constrained motion.
Derive work-energy and impulse-momentum relations and apply them to extended systems.
Calculate inertia, torque and angular momentum and solve elementary rigid-body rotational problems.
Derive harmonic and damped oscillator models and verify supplied analytic solutions by differentiation.

practice: Derive and solve mechanical models and compare predictions with trajectory or oscillation data.

includes: Coulomb fields and electric potential for discrete charges; magnetic forces; flux and induction in elementary geometries.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Elementary Electric and Magnetic Fields

outcomes.description: Calculate discrete-charge fields and potentials and explain electric energy and conductor behavior.
Predict magnetic forces and charged-particle motion using vector directions and algebraic models.
Apply flux-change and induction models to simple loops and explain energy conservation and sign conventions.

practice: Solve charge and induction problems and compare field-line representations with quantitative predictions.

includes: Kirchhoff laws and resistive networks; capacitors, inductors and stated transient models; safe low-voltage circuit measurement.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electric Circuits

outcomes.description: Solve resistive networks using current and voltage laws and calculate power and equivalent circuits.
Analyze capacitor and inductor energy and apply explicitly stated exponential transient models.
Use meters and oscilloscopes to measure low-voltage circuits and account for loading and bandwidth.

practice: Construct and characterize safe resistive and storage-element circuits with uncertainty and loading analysis.

includes: Temperature, heat and thermodynamic laws; gas processes, cycles and entropy; elementary kinetic-gas and equipartition models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Macroscopic thermal behavior and microscopic interpretation.
decks.title: Thermal Physics

outcomes.description: Apply the first and second laws with explicit system boundaries and reversible or irreversible processes.
Calculate work, heat, entropy changes and engine or refrigerator efficiencies for elementary cycles.
Derive elementary kinetic-gas pressure and interpret equipartition and heat-capacity models with stated limits.

practice: Analyze thermal cycles and calorimetric data and compare microscopic and macroscopic energy accounting.

includes: Harmonic and traveling-wave representations; interference, standing waves and resonance; acoustic intensity and Doppler models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Propagation and superposition across physical media.
decks.title: Waves and Acoustics

outcomes.description: Relate amplitude, phase, frequency, wavelength and propagation speed in sinusoidal wave models.
Calculate interference, standing-wave modes and driven resonance in elementary systems.
Apply acoustic intensity, impedance and Doppler models and identify their linear-regime limitations.

practice: Measure resonances and wave interference and explain deviations from ideal linear models.

includes: Reflection and refraction; lenses, mirrors and imaging instruments; aberrations, apertures and introductory resolution limits.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: An accessible route to optical imaging.
decks.title: Geometrical Optics

outcomes.description: Construct and calculate reflected and refracted ray paths and paraxial image formation.
Analyze lens and mirror combinations, magnification and elementary microscope or telescope designs.
Diagnose aberration, aperture and ray-model limitations and distinguish them from detector errors.

practice: Build or simulate imaging systems and measure magnification, focus and aberration.

includes: Lorentz transformations and simultaneity; Minkowski intervals and four-vector notation taught locally; relativistic energy and momentum.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Space, time and motion beyond Galilean models.
decks.title: Special Relativity

outcomes.description: Derive Lorentz transformations and solve simultaneity, time-dilation and length-contraction problems.
Calculate spacetime intervals and elementary four-vector invariants and classify causal relationships.
Apply relativistic energy-momentum conservation to decays, collisions and threshold problems.

practice: Resolve relativistic thought experiments using spacetime diagrams and invariant calculations.

includes: Photoelectric, spectral and interference evidence; explicit two-state amplitude models; quantized atomic transitions and uncertainty.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Phenomena

outcomes.description: Use photoelectric, diffraction and spectral evidence to distinguish classical and quantum explanations.
Calculate probabilities in explicitly taught two-state amplitude models and explain measurement and interference.
Apply quantized energy-transition and uncertainty models while identifying their domain and limitations.

practice: Analyze historical quantum experiments and solve two-path and two-state prediction problems.

includes: Variational principles and constrained Lagrangian dynamics; Hamiltonian mechanics; canonical transformations and integrable motion.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive Euler-Lagrange equations and conservation laws for constrained mechanical systems.
Construct Hamiltonians and analyze phase-space flow and Poisson brackets.
Use canonical transformations and action-angle variables in elementary integrable systems.

practice: Derive equivalent dynamical formulations and analyze constrained and coupled mechanical systems.

includes: Electrostatic boundary-value problems; magnetostatics and materials; Maxwell equations and electromagnetic waves; elementary radiation.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electromagnetic Fields

outcomes.description: Solve electrostatic boundary problems using potentials, multipoles and uniqueness arguments.
Derive magnetostatic fields and analyze bound currents and linear magnetic media.
Derive wave, energy and boundary relations from Maxwell equations in vacuum and simple media.
Calculate elementary dipole radiation and distinguish near, intermediate and radiation fields.

practice: Derive and solve boundary and radiation problems with conservation and limiting-case checks.

includes: AC response and filters; bounded diode, transistor and amplifier models; sampling, conversion and acquisition electronics.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Electronic systems for amplification and measurement.
decks.title: Electronics

outcomes.description: Derive transient and frequency responses of linear circuits using differential and transform methods.
Design amplifiers and switching circuits using explicit device models and assess nonlinear limits.
Design elementary acquisition chains and analyze sampling, quantization, loading and bandwidth.

practice: Build or simulate a sensor amplifier and acquisition chain and characterize its response and failures.

includes: Thermodynamic potentials and Legendre transforms; Maxwell and response relations; phase coexistence and stability.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Thermodynamics

outcomes.description: Derive thermodynamic potentials and select natural variables for constrained equilibrium problems.
Derive Maxwell relations and connect heat capacities, compressibilities and expansion coefficients.
Analyze stability and phase coexistence using thermodynamic curvature and equilibrium conditions.

practice: Prove thermodynamic identities and solve stability and phase-transition problems under different constraints.

includes: Microcanonical, canonical and grand-canonical ensembles; classical phase-space partitions; fluctuations and response.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Classical Statistical Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive equilibrium ensembles and justify their constraints and thermodynamic relationships.
Calculate classical partition functions and thermodynamic observables with correct phase-space counting.
Derive fluctuation-response relations and assess finite-size and ensemble-equivalence limitations.

practice: Derive ensemble predictions for gases, oscillators and simple interacting models.

includes: Hilbert-space operators and measurement; one-dimensional Schrodinger problems; orbital and spin angular momentum and tensor products; variational and elementary perturbative methods.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics

outcomes.description: Calculate state evolution, measurement probabilities and uncertainty using finite and wavefunction operator representations.
Solve canonical one-dimensional Schrodinger boundary problems and interpret bound states and tunneling.
Use angular-momentum algebra, spin and tensor-product states in elementary atomic and coupled-state problems.
Apply variational and nondegenerate perturbative approximations and assess their validity.

practice: Derive spectra and measurement predictions and compare exact and approximate quantum solutions.

includes: Continuum conservation and stress; Euler and Navier-Stokes equations; viscous flow, dimensionless groups and instability limits.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Fluid Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive mass, momentum and energy balances and explain constitutive and continuum assumptions.
Solve elementary inviscid and viscous flows with appropriate initial and boundary conditions.
Use nondimensionalization to assess regimes, boundary layers and the onset of instability or turbulence.

practice: Derive flow models and compare analytic solutions and scaling estimates with fluid-measurement data.

includes: Stress and strain tensors; linear elastic constitutive laws and boundary problems; elastic energy, buckling and failure criteria.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Deformation and stability of solid continua.
decks.title: Elasticity and Solid Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive small-strain kinematics and stress balance and distinguish isotropic and anisotropic constitutive laws.
Solve elementary tension, torsion and bending boundary problems with compatible stress and displacement conditions.
Analyze elastic energy, buckling and elementary yield or fracture criteria with their limitations.

practice: Derive deformation models and compare stiffness, buckling and failure predictions for simple structures.

includes: Scalar diffraction and Fourier optics; temporal and spatial coherence; transverse polarization and optical interference.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Wave foundations of imaging and interference.
decks.title: Wave Optics

outcomes.description: Derive elementary diffraction and imaging relations using scalar wave and Fourier approximations.
Calculate interference visibility from coherence models and distinguish temporal and spatial coherence.
Use transverse-field and Jones-vector models to analyze polarization transformations and measurements.

practice: Analyze diffraction and polarization experiments and quantify approximation and coherence limits.

includes: State-space and transfer-function models; controllability and observability; feedback stability and controller design.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Reusable theory for regulated dynamical systems.
decks.title: Control Theory

outcomes.description: Convert explicit dynamical models between state-space and transfer representations and assess controllability and observability.
Analyze closed-loop stability and robustness using poles, frequency response and stability margins.
Design PID and state-feedback controllers for specified models and evaluate tracking and disturbance tradeoffs.

practice: Derive and tune controllers for supplied plant models using hand calculations and explicit performance bounds.

includes: Crystal reciprocal space and lattice vibrations; Bloch bands; Fermi occupation as an explicit bounded model; magnetic and superconducting phenomenology.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Condensed-Matter Physics

outcomes.description: Derive lattice normal modes and relate reciprocal-space structure to phonons and diffraction.
Derive elementary Bloch and band models and distinguish metals, semiconductors and insulators.
Use the explicitly taught Fermi occupation model to calculate electronic populations and low-temperature responses.
Explain elementary magnetic and superconducting order using bounded models and experimental signatures.

practice: Derive simple band and lattice models and interpret transport, heat-capacity and ordering data.

includes: Carrier statistics and drift-diffusion; junction electrostatics and recombination; transistor and optoelectronic device principles.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Semiconductor Physics

outcomes.description: Derive carrier balance and elementary drift-diffusion relations with mobility and recombination assumptions.
Calculate depletion, built-in potentials and elementary diode behavior from semiconductor junction models.
Explain transistor control and elementary photodetection or emission using band and carrier mechanisms.

practice: Derive device characteristics and compare model predictions with measured or supplied current-voltage data.

includes: Nuclear binding and structure models; decay, scattering, fission and fusion; radiation interactions and detectors.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Structure and transformations of atomic nuclei.
decks.title: Nuclear Physics

outcomes.description: Compare liquid-drop and shell models and calculate elementary binding and nuclear-state consequences.
Analyze decay chains and nuclear reaction energetics, thresholds and elementary cross-section models.
Explain radiation-matter interactions and interpret detector efficiency, resolution and counting uncertainty.

practice: Analyze nuclear spectra and reaction datasets and compare model explanations under radiation-safety constraints.

includes: Standard Model particle content and interactions; conservation and discrete symmetries; relativistic collision and decay signatures.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Elementary Particle Physics

outcomes.description: Classify particles and interactions and explain the empirical organization of the Standard Model.
Apply conserved quantum numbers and discrete-symmetry tests to allowed and forbidden processes.
Calculate invariant masses, decay kinematics and thresholds and interpret elementary collision signatures.

practice: Reconstruct particle processes from event data and distinguish kinematic evidence from interaction-model assumptions.

includes: Coordinates, fluxes, magnitudes and distance observations; celestial orbit models; planets, stars and galaxies from observational evidence.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Astronomy

outcomes.description: Interpret astronomical coordinates, images, fluxes, magnitudes and elementary distance indicators.
Apply elementary orbital and transit models to solar-system and exoplanet observations.
Compare planetary, stellar and galactic populations while accounting for detection and selection effects.

practice: Analyze public imaging, transit and catalog data and document observational selection limits.

includes: Radiation and stellar structure models; stellar evolution and remnants using bounded microphysics; galaxy dynamics and mass inference.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Physical modeling of stars and galaxies.
decks.title: Astrophysics

outcomes.description: Derive elementary hydrostatic and radiative stellar-structure equations using explicitly specified opacity and energy models.
Explain stellar evolution and remnant formation using energy balance, nuclear-fuel and stated degeneracy models.
Analyze galactic orbital dynamics and infer mass distributions while assessing equilibrium and selection assumptions.

practice: Derive stellar scaling models and analyze public stellar and galactic data against competing physical explanations.

includes: Degenerate and time-dependent perturbation theory; scattering and partial waves; density operators, entanglement and identical particles.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive degenerate and time-dependent perturbative predictions, transition rates and selection rules.
Calculate elementary scattering amplitudes and cross sections using Born and partial-wave methods.
Use density operators and symmetrized states to analyze mixed states, entanglement and identical particles.

practice: Derive transition and scattering predictions and solve mixed-state and identical-particle problems.

includes: Density-operator ensembles; Bose and Fermi gases and condensation; interacting models, mean field and critical scaling foundations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Statistical Physics

outcomes.description: Derive quantum equilibrium ensembles and trace-based thermodynamic identities.
Derive Bose and Fermi distributions and analyze degeneracy and condensation regimes.
Analyze elementary interacting models, mean-field transitions and fluctuations near criticality.

practice: Derive quantum-gas thermodynamics and compare mean-field predictions with fluctuation-sensitive examples.

includes: Lorentzian spacetime and equivalence; Einstein equations and stress-energy; black-hole, weak-field and gravitational-wave solutions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: General Relativity

outcomes.description: Relate local inertial motion, geodesics and tidal effects to Lorentzian geometry.
Derive Einstein equations from the stated field action and analyze stress-energy conservation.
Solve and interpret representative spherical, weak-field and linear gravitational-wave problems.

practice: Derive relativistic solutions and calculate observable orbital, lensing and wave effects.

includes: Classical field actions and canonical quantization; propagators and perturbative amplitudes; regularization and renormalization; local gauge symmetry.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Field Theory

outcomes.description: Derive field equations and quantize free scalar, spinor and vector fields with symmetry constraints.
Construct propagators and calculate elementary perturbative scattering amplitudes using Feynman rules.
Regularize and renormalize representative one-loop calculations and interpret scale dependence.
Derive elementary gauge interactions and explain gauge fixing, conserved currents and symmetry breaking.

practice: Complete field-quantization and scattering derivations and a controlled one-loop renormalization calculation.

includes: Homogeneous cosmological dynamics; thermal history and relics; linear perturbations, structure growth and cosmological evidence.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Dynamics and history of the universe.
decks.title: Cosmology

outcomes.description: Derive Friedmann dynamics and cosmological distance relations and assess background-model assumptions.
Calculate equilibrium and freeze-out scales and explain nucleosynthesis and recombination using specified reaction models.
Derive elementary linear growth equations and connect perturbations to structure and background-radiation observations.

practice: Derive cosmological predictions and compare parameter-dependent models with public background and expansion data.

includes: Kinetic plasma descriptions and shielding; collective waves and instabilities; magnetohydrodynamics and confinement limits.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Plasma Physics

outcomes.description: Derive elementary kinetic and screening models and justify fluid reductions and collision assumptions.
Derive representative plasma dispersion relations and assess damping and instability mechanisms.
Analyze magnetohydrodynamic equilibria and waves and explain elementary confinement and reconnection limits.

practice: Derive plasma-wave and equilibrium models and diagnose unstable regimes from specified parameters.

includes: Second-quantized interacting models; Green functions and linear response; magnetism, superfluidity and superconducting mean-field theory.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Collective quantum phenomena from interacting particles.
decks.title: Many-Body Physics

outcomes.description: Construct and manipulate second-quantized Hamiltonians for interacting lattice and continuum systems.
Derive elementary Green-function and linear-response expressions and connect them to observables.
Analyze representative magnetic, superfluid and superconducting phases using controlled mean-field approximations.

practice: Derive many-body response and ordering predictions and identify where approximation assumptions fail.

includes: Detector response and calibration; noise spectra, filtering and lock-in detection; model fitting and uncertainty budgets.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Experimental Physics Methods

outcomes.description: Calibrate detector response and quantify nonlinearity, drift, efficiency and systematic uncertainty.
Analyze noise spectra and implement filtering or lock-in extraction without invalid sampling assumptions.
Fit physical models, propagate parameter uncertainty and distinguish statistical from systematic discrepancies.

practice: Build a reproducible acquisition and analysis pipeline for a weak-signal experiment or instrument-equivalent dataset.

includes: Coarse-graining and scaling operators; renormalization flows and fixed points; universality and finite-size scaling.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: A research continuation in collective scale-dependent behavior.
decks.title: Renormalization and Critical Systems

outcomes.description: Construct elementary coarse-graining transformations and classify relevant, irrelevant and marginal perturbations.
Analyze renormalization flows and fixed points and derive elementary critical-exponent relationships.
Estimate scaling behavior from simulated models and assess universality and finite-size corrections.

practice: Implement a coarse-graining or lattice-model study and test scaling collapse against alternative universality claims.
